title: Ada and the Border
premise: Tamsin Joubert, a whistle-blower living under four names since exposing a covert data-trafficking operation, receives a meeting invitation from a handler who died six months ago. Following it into the border city of Virelle, Tamsin discovers the 'incident' that forced them to run was staged by their own agency, and the dead handler's message is bait set by Director Ilse Marchetti, who needs the one unredacted file in Tamsin's head before an international summit ratifies the very surveillance pact Tamsin exposed. Hunted by Marchetti's fixer and shadowed by a journalist who may be ally or trap, Tamsin must decide whether loyalty to the people who burned them is worth trading away the truth. In the end, Tasmir—under their real name, Nadia Okafor—broadcasts the file during the summit's opening session, sacrificing anonymity forever but shattering the pact and forcing Marchetti's arrest.
about_author: M. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former policy analyst who spent three years working near international border commissions before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to make them disappear.

chapters.title: Four Names, No Sleep
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. Living as 'Ruth Calloway' in a coastal boarding house, Tamsin catalogs their nightly rituals of invisibility until an encrypted invitation arrives—from a handler confirmed dead, scheduling a meeting tomorrow at the Virelle border crossing. The beat is dread sharpening into fatal curiosity: someone knows exactly where they are.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. Against every instinct, Tamsin travels to Virelle and waits at the meeting point, where instead of a ghost they find journalist Priya Anand holding the handler's notebook—and a bullet meant for her misses them both. The emotional beat: terror fusing with the first flicker of alliance.

chapters.title: What the Notebook Says
chapters.summary: POV: Priya. Through Priya's eyes, we learn the notebook implicates Director Ilse Marchetti in staging the incident that destroyed Tamsin's life—a false flag to bury the whistle-blowing. Priya wants a story; Tamsin wants survival. The beat: wary negotiation between two people who need each other's secrets.

chapters.title: The Fixer Arrives
chapters.summary: POV: Anton Reyes, Marchetti's fixer. Reyes arrives in Virelle with orders to retrieve the file 'clean'—no bodies if possible. He traces Tamsin through a pawned burner phone, revealing how porous their four-name armor really is. The beat: cold professional menace, and his private doubt about what he's retrieving.

chapters.title: The Safehouse That Isn't
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. A former agency contact offers shelter, but Tamsin realizes mid-night that the safehouse is wired—the contact sold them out. Escaping through flooded backstreets, they lose the notebook but keep the memory: the file exists only in their head. The beat: betrayal confirming that belonging was always a lure.

chapters.title: Marchetti's Offer
chapters.summary: POV: Ilse Marchetti. In her summit-bound motorcade, Marchetti reflects on building the surveillance pact on the bones of the incident she ordered, then makes Tamsin an offer via hijacked screen: full restoration of identity, protection, a life—in exchange for the file before the summit convenes. The beat: seductive power, almost convincing.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Priced
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. Tempted, Tamsin digs into their own past and finds the handler's last hidden message: proof that colleagues Tamsin still loves were complicit—or coerced. Loyalty curdles into grief. The beat: the quiet devastation of learning the people you protected chose the system over you.

chapters.title: The Summit Eve
chapters.summary: POV: Priya and Reyes alternating. On the eve of the signing, Priya plans a broadcast from inside the press pavilion while Reyes closes the net, catching Tamsin at the perimeter—but hesitates when he sees the file's contents name his own brother among the trafficked. The beat: the hunter's crisis of conscience.

chapters.title: Nadia Okafor
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. Captured and brought before Marchetti, Tamsin discards all four names and claims their real one aloud for the first time in two years. When Marchetti orders the file extracted by force, Reyes turns, and Priya's broadcast goes live mid-struggle. The beat: identity reclaimed at gunpoint—the novel's climax.

chapters.title: After the Border
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. The pact collapses; Marchetti is arrested, though the machine she built grinds on without her. Tamsin, now publicly Nadia Okafor, sleeps through a night for the first time since the incident—not because the world is safe, but because hiding is over. The beat: costly, imperfect peace.
